tip: 'Sampai-sampai' = 'so much so that': 'sampai-sampai dia menangis' = to the point that he cried.
Adjective + '-nya' opens a comment: 'anehnya' = the strange thing is..., 'lucunya' = the funny part is...
'Ber-' + number = a group of people: 'kami berdua' = the two of us, 'mereka bertiga' = the three of them.
'Makin lama makin' X = more and more X over time: 'makin lama makin besar' = keeps getting bigger.
Commands drop the 'men-' prefix: 'ceritakan!' = tell it! In a statement the full form returns: 'dia menceritakan...'
'Pun' is written separately after question words: 'apa pun' = anything/whatever, 'siapa pun' = anyone.
With a negative, 'satu' + noun + 'pun' = not even one: 'satu lembar pun' = not even one bill.
'Sekali pun' (two words) = even once: 'belum terlambat sekali pun' = never late, not even once.
'Se-' + adjective + 'apa pun' = no matter how: 'sesulit apa pun' = no matter how difficult.
'Bahkan' = even, introduces the strongest example: 'bahkan pedagang pun' = even the vendors.
'Cuma' = only/just, the everyday spoken word; 'hanya' means the same but sounds more careful.
'Hanya' X 'yang' ... = only X (and no one else): 'hanya penumpang ini yang boleh masuk' = only these passengers may enter.
Question word + 'saja' = any-: 'kapan saja' = anytime, 'apa saja' = anything, 'siapa saja' = anyone.
'Baru saja' = just (moments ago): 'baru saja tidur' = just fell asleep.
'Anggap saja' = just consider it: 'anggap saja rumah sendiri' = make yourself at home.
X + 'saja' can mean 'it's just (my) X': 'perasaan saya saja' = it's just my imagination.
'Akhirnya ... juga' = finally, at last: 'akhirnya lulus juga' = finally passed (after all that).
'Belum ... juga' = still not, with a hint of impatience: 'belum diantar juga' = still hasn't been delivered.
'Juga' can soften an opinion: 'enak juga' = actually pretty nice (a mild, pleasant surprise).
'Bukan hanya' X, 'tetapi' Y 'juga' = not only X, but also Y.
'Sendiri' after a verb phrase = by oneself: 'mengatur uangnya sendiri' = manage her money herself.
'Sendiri' can mean 'by itself': 'mati sendiri' = went off on its own, nobody touched it.
Noun + '-nya sendiri' = one's own: 'meja kerjanya sendiri' = his own desk.
'Pula' = as well/what's more, a slightly bookish 'juga': 'dekat pantai pula' = close to the beach too.
'Memang' = indeed/admittedly, confirms a fact: 'memang saya yang salah' = it really was my fault.
'Soal' X = when it comes to X: 'soal macet' = as for traffic jams.
'Sih' is a little spoken word you'll hear everywhere: 'bagus sih' = it's good, I admit. Recognize it; no need to use it.
'Asal' = as long as: 'di mana saja asal tidak menutup jalan' = anywhere, provided it doesn't block the road.
Noun + 'pun' = even: 'musim kemarau pun' = even (in) the dry season.
'Saja' comes after the phrase it limits – 'lima menit saja', not 'saja lima menit'. The reverse of English 'just five minutes'.
